nodes.name: Ni substrate pretreatment
nodes.procedure: The Ni-based substrates were soaked in a 1 M HNO₃ mild acidic solution for 10 minutes before cell assembly or catalyst loading, followed by thorough washing with DI water.
nodes.source_text: The Ni-based substrates were soaked in a 1 M HNO₃ mild acidic solution for at 10 minutes before cell assembly or catalyst loading, followed by thorough washing with DI water.

nodes.name: Catalyst ink preparation
nodes.procedure: The catalyst ink was prepared by mixing catalysts with D2020 Nafion in a 1:3 (w:w) ratio of deionized (DI) water to 1-propanol (nPA), followed by sonication in an ice bath for over 30 minutes and subsequent aging (stirring at room temperature) for approximately one day. For the ink composition, Pt/C was prepared with a solid content of 4% and an ionomer-to-catalyst ratio of 0.5, while NiFe, NiO, and Co₃O₄ inks had a solid content of 2% and an ionomer-to-metal ratio of 0.3.

nodes.name: Catalyst coated electrode fabrication
nodes.procedure: The ink was then applied onto nickel foam via hand-spraying. After spray coating, the electrodes were dried at 60°C for at least 15 minutes, followed by additional drying at room temperature for over 24 hours to ensure proper adhesion and solvent evaporation.

nodes.description: Baseline HER and OER performance in zero-gap AWE cell - nickel foam electrodes (catalyst-free reference)
nodes.source_text: Electrochemical analysis comparing cathode and anode behavior reveals consistently greater overpotential for the cathode (HER) than for the anode (OER) across all current densities (Fig. 1b). ... higher charge transfer resistance (0.95 vs. 0.27 Ω cm²) (Fig. 1c) ... steeper Tafel slope (143 vs. 51 mV dec⁻¹, Fig. S9)

nodes.description: HER performance - Pt/C at cathode with bare Ni foam anode (Pt/C cathode control)
nodes.source_text: Pt/C (cathode) control case—where Pt/C was introduced only at the cathode—the HER Tafel slope reached 39.6 mV dec⁻¹ and the HER kinetic overpotential was 78 mV ... potential gains of 50–55 mV for HER at low current densities

nodes.description: OER performance with NiFe anode catalyst in AWE cell
nodes.source_text: NiFe catalyst (1.0 mg cm⁻²) was used at the anode... OER Tafel slope was measured as 47.5 mV dec⁻¹, and the OER kinetic overpotential as 253 mV... potential gains of 60-67 mV for OER

nodes.description: Nickel foam long-term stability test at 2.0 V up to 150h
nodes.source_text: After a 24-hour voltage held at 2.0 V, polarization curves showed increased electrode potential... Over 150 hours, cathode activity initially improved before slightly declining, while the anode showed early degradation followed by partial recovery

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES analysis of nickel foam cathode revealed shifts in the white-line peak to higher energies with increased intensity after 24h, indicating oxidation state increase and surface Ni(OH)₂ formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analysis revealed shifts in the white-line peak (1s → 4p) to higher energies with increased intensity (Fig. 4b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS of nickel foam cathode showed slight increase in Ni-Ni radial distance after 24h with preserved intensity, indicating bulk metallic structure preservation with surface modification.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni K-edge Fourier transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) analysis showed a slight increase in the radial distance of the Ni–Ni peak, with no significant loss in intensity (Fig. 4c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge WT-EXAFS of nickel foam cathode identified Ni-M multi-scattering signal at ~3.5 Å after 150h, indicating metal impurity incorporation from KOH electrolyte.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Wavelet transform (WT) analysis identified a multi-scattering Ni–M signal (~3.5 Å) ... indicating metal impurities (Fe, Al, Zn, Mn, Cu, Cr) from the KOH electrolyte (Fig. 4d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L₃-edge XANES of Pt/C cathode indicated decreased oxidation state after 24h voltage hold with sustained white-line peak intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt L-edge XANES analysis indicated a decrease in the oxidation state of Pt, with sustained white-line peak intensity (Fig. 4f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L-edge WT-EXAFS of Pt/C cathode revealed multi-scattering signal near 4.5 Å (Pt-M-Pt bonds) when NiFe anode used simultaneously, indicating interactions with migrated metal species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: WT analysis, which revealed a multi-scattering signal near 4.5 Å corresponding to Pt–M–Pt bonds, indicating potential interactions between Pt and migrated metal species (Fig. 4f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge XANES of NiFe anode showed decreased pre-edge and increased white-line peak intensity after 24h, indicating transformation into Ni(Fe)OOH structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe K-edge XANES revealed a decreased pre-edge and increased white-line peak intensity, indicating the transformation of NiFe alloy into a Ni(Fe)OOH structure (Fig. 4g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge WT-EXAFS of NiFe anode confirmed strong single-scattering signal at 1.7 Å indicating coordination with O-based species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: WT-EXAFS further confirmed these ligand interactions, with a strong single-scattering signal at 1.7 Å (Fig. 4g).
